descriptions.text: Fake Market. Lost: 4.1M VUSD, 7.35M XCN, 5K DAI, 0.23 WBTC, 50K USDT (>$3.8M USD)

Another Compound v2 fork that just can't catch a break, Onyx Protocol, has been exploited again. This time, the damage tally stands at a cool $3.8 million, siphoned off by the same high-profile vulnerability that bit them late last year.

The root cause was unverified user input during the liquidation process. Specifically, key parameters of the liquidateWithSingleRepay function in the NFTLiquidation contract were controllable by the attacker, allowing manipulation of the extraRepayAmount variable through the repayAmount parameter. By exploiting this, the attacker was able to liquidate all collateral with just one token. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://etherscan.io/tx/0x46567c731c4f4f7e27c4ce591f0aebdeb2d9ae1038237a0134de7b13e63d8729 Analysis: https://medium.com/coinmonks/decoding-onyxdaos-4m-exploit-e1858d35b3e6

Onyx protocol suffered a security breach, resulting in a loss of over $3.8 million. The attacker exploited a known precision issue in the Compound V2 code. Additionally, the NFTLiquidation contract failed to properly validate untrusted user input, allowing the attacker to inflate the self-liquidation reward amount, which further worsened the losses.

Onyx V2 on Ethereum was exploited on September 26, 2024, via a liquidation logic flaw in an NFT market. Approximately $3.8 million was drained by manipulating the collateral exchange rate and abusing unchecked inputs in the liquidation contract. Unchecked input validation in the NFT liquidation contract enabled fabricated excess repayment. The attacker exploited a low-liquidity market and manipulated the collateral exchange rate, triggering liquidation and seizing disproportionate collateral.

OnyxDAO, a Compound V2 fork, was exploited for over $3.8M after an attacker manipulated oETH exchange rates via precision loss and used flawed NFTLiquidation inputs to seize collateral with minimal repayment. The protocol's Compound V2-based contracts suffered from an exchange rate precision bug, particularly in low-liquidity markets. The NFTLiquidation contract failed to validate repayAmount and extraRepayAmount, enabling near-zero-cost self-liquidation by the attacker after exchange rate manipulation.

The Onyx protocol was hacked for a second time by attackers taking advantage of known bugs in forks of the Compound Finance project. Projects regularly fail to patch these bugs, despite many instances of multi-million dollar hacks affecting Compound forks in the past. Onyx apparently didn't learn their lesson the first time around, when they were exploited for $2 million in November 2023 by an attacker taking advantage of a known vulnerability affecting empty markets on the protocol. This same bug seems to have contributed to this exploit, although Onyx has claimed the hack was due to a separate vulnerability in an NFT liquidation contract .
